references.text: The Lord declares himself to be a jealous God who will not tolerate idolatry, the same theme Joshua warns the people about.
The Lord is called 'Jealous' as a name, and it is emphasized that he is a jealous God, parallel to Joshua's description.
God's holiness is the basis for his demand that the people be holy, the same theme concerning God's holiness.
The Lord is described as a consuming fire and a jealous God, the same characteristic found in Joshua.
It warns that the Lord's jealousy can lead to destruction if the people turn to other gods.
The question of who can stand before the holy God the Lord reflects the same theme concerning God's holiness.
The seraphs cry out, 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts,' which emphasizes God's absolute holiness.
The Lord is described as a jealous and avenging God, parallel to Joshua's description of God's jealousy.
God is described as a consuming fire, emphasizing his holiness and that one must serve him with reverence.
The Lord will not forgive transgressions because his name is in the angel, parallel to the idea that God will not bear with sin.
